Fields already filled in below are derived from pinned repo facts (splits, methodology-contract.json, the Layer 1-3 outputs), not placeholders.

result_revision.change_summary: Initial candidate AirfRANS AoA-extrapolation submission for Transolver++ trained on the official aoa_train partition with a validation holdout carved from it.

methodology.record_note: Adapted from the official Transolver++ reference implementation (https://github.com/thuml/Transolver_plus/blob/main/models/Transolver_plus.py). Submitter-reported DDP adaptation note: the original implementation uses sequence parallelism (dist_nn.all_reduce inside Physics_Attention_1D_Eidetic) to synchronize attention tokens across devices, assuming one large spatial graph partitioned across GPUs. This pipeline instead uses standard Distributed Data Parallelism: because AirfRANS meshes have highly variable node counts (preventing batch stacking), each GPU processes exactly one intact mesh per step, so the entire graph for a sample fits in one GPU's VRAM. Leaving the cross-GPU all_reduce active under this DDP setup would aggregate attention tokens across independent meshes on different GPUs, cross-contaminating physical/geometric features between unrelated samples. The submitter therefore bypassed the dist_nn.all_reduce synchronization in the forward pass; global synchronization is instead handled correctly and exclusively by the DDP backend during the backward pass (gradient reduction), preserving strict per-sample independence in the forward computation. find_unused_parameters=True was set in the DDP wrapper to handle the idle condition-embedding layer present in the original architecture without structural deletions. Inference note: Physics_Attention_1D_Eidetic samples Gumbel noise in its slice weights even in eval mode, so the inference script reseeds torch (seed 42) before every case's forward pass; predictions are bit-for-bit reproducible per case.

architecture.description: Transolver++ (Physics_Attention_1D_Eidetic variant with Gumbel-softmax adaptive-temperature slice weighting): an input MLP embeds 8 per-node channels (6 broadcast global case parameters + 2D native coordinates) into a 256-wide hidden representation, followed by 5 Transolver++ blocks (LayerNorm -> physics attention with 8 heads / 32 slices -> LayerNorm -> MLP, residual throughout), with a final linear head on the last block producing all 3 output channels (Ux, Uy, p) in one forward pass. A per-case scalar 'condition' embedding exists in the architecture but is never populated (always None) in this deployment, so it is architecturally present but functionally inactive; it was kept only to satisfy DistributedDataParallel's find_unused_parameters requirement.

components.role: Embeds the 8 input channels (6 broadcast global params + 2 coordinates) into the 256-wide hidden representation.
components.description: Single-layer preprocessing MLP (8 -> 512 -> 256, GELU), no residual layers.

components.role: 5-layer adaptive-slicing physics-attention core; the final block's linear head produces the 3 output channels (Ux, Uy, p).
components.description: 5 stacked Transolver_plus_block modules (LayerNorm, 8-head/32-slice Gumbel-softmax adaptive physics attention, LayerNorm, MLP, residual connections throughout); the last block additionally applies a LayerNorm + Linear(256, 3) output head.

components.role: Dead/inactive layer: a Linear(3, 256) condition embedding and a small learnable placeholder bias, present in the architecture but never exercised because the model is always called with condition=None in this deployment.
components.description: Kept only so DistributedDataParallel's find_unused_parameters handling does not require structurally deleting this head from the reference implementation.

input_features.name: global_case_parameters
input_features.description: Inlet velocity, angle of attack, and 4 NACA shape parameters, standardized and broadcast to every native mesh point.

predicted_fields.description: Cartesian velocity (Ux, Uy) on every native 2D flow-domain point.
Kinematic pressure on every native 2D flow-domain point.

Airfoil-curve pressure, selected from the domain pressure prediction at the native surface points and reorganized onto the airfoil's native point order (methodology-contract.json explicitly allows this: 'may be derived by selecting the corresponding output').

data_handling.normalization: Mean/std standardization fitted on the 724 training cases only (validation and test excluded): global params mean=[62.584365, 4.750972, 2.656636, 4.361279, -0.175896, 12.584866] std=[17.970328, 4.315000, 1.783677, 2.270842, 0.860530, 4.298528]; coordinates mean=[0.500380, 0.011412] std=[0.704417, 0.336095]; targets (u, v, p) mean=[43.025150, 10.431554, -333.498579] std=[29.278551, 28.157594, 2413.484591]. Predictions are denormalized (pred * std + mean) before packing onto native points.
data_handling.preprocessing: Each case's complete native internal-mesh point cloud and (u, v, p) fields are read directly from a pre-processed AirfRANS pickle (X_original, fields); no remeshing, cropping, or geometric preprocessing.
data_handling.sampling: None: the complete native point set for every case is used for both training supervision and inference. Batch size is fixed at exactly 1 full mesh per GPU step (no subsampling), because AirfRANS meshes have highly variable node counts that prevent standard batch stacking.

stages.description: Single from-scratch run. The official 804-case AirfRANS aoa_train partition was split into 724 training and 80 validation cases (val_fraction 0.1, seed 42); the official 196-case AoA-extrapolation test split was not used for training, normalization, or checkpoint selection.

loss.description: Mean squared error between predicted and normalized ground-truth (Ux, Uy, p), averaged over all native points in the mesh.
loss.weighting: Uniform per-point MSE; no field-wise or spatial weighting.

optimizers.name: AdamW
optimizers.schedule: Constant learning rate, no scheduler. AdamW weight_decay=1e-4.

batch.unit: cases per optimizer step (1 intact mesh per GPU on 2 GPUs, DDP)

compute.measurement_notes: From the training log ('Training complete in 12h 33m 8.34s'), 2-way DistributedDataParallel, ~113.2s/epoch across 400 epochs.

checkpoints.bytes_description: Raw PyTorch state_dict (transolver_3ch_aoa_best.pt), saved whenever the validation loss improved.
checkpoints.role: Single checkpoint; one forward pass produces all three predicted fields (Ux, Uy, p).
checkpoints.selection_rule: Lowest validation loss over the fixed 400-epoch schedule (reached at epoch 388), measured on the 80-case validation holdout drawn from aoa_train; the 196-case AoA-extrapolation test split was never used for selection.

inference_compute.measurement_notes: Single uninterrupted run over all 196 AoA-extrapolation cases (batch size 1, sequential, single GPU), covering data loading, normalization, GPU transfer and the forward pass, with per-case reseeding. Excludes plotting and the separate packing step onto native mesh points.

domain_input.notes: Entity counts reuse the official 196-case AoA-extrapolation evaluation split's native point-count distribution as a representative proxy; per-case counts for the 724-case training subset of aoa_train were not separately enumerated.

domain_supervision.notes: Entity counts reuse the official 196-case AoA-extrapolation evaluation split's native point-count distribution as a representative proxy; per-case counts for the 724-case training subset of aoa_train were not separately enumerated.

inference.note: Inference representation itself (native mesh, full coverage, identity mapping, zero unmapped/extrapolated) is already known from Layers 1-2 and will be filled in automatically -- only the TRAINING representation above needs your input.
